title: NHS strikes 2022-24 — the biggest wave since 1948
hook: Between December 2022 and September 2024, junior doctors, consultants, nurses, ambulance crews and radiographers collectively struck for longer than in any period since the NHS was created.
lede: The Royal College of Nursing struck for the first time in its history on 15 December 2022. Junior doctors (resident doctors from 2024) struck for 44 days between March 2023 and July 2024. Consultants struck. Ambulance staff struck. The cumulative cost of cancelled appointments and cover payments exceeded £3bn. Wes Streeting closed the junior-doctors dispute on 16 September 2024 with a 22.3% cumulative pay deal.
body_md:
**The RCN, December 2022.** The Royal College of Nursing, a professional body that historically refused strike action, balloted in late 2022 over below-inflation pay awards and workforce attrition. 15 December 2022 saw the first-ever RCN strike — pickets at every major hospital, elective surgery cancelled, minimum safe staffing maintained. Pay demands: 5% above RPI inflation (around 17% in cash). Settled February 2023 with a 5% cash award and a £1,655 lump-sum for Agenda for Change bands 2-8a.

**Junior doctors — the long campaign.** BMA junior-doctor members balloted for strike action in March 2023, demanding 'full pay restoration' — a 35% increase to restore 2008 real-terms value. Successive 3-day, then 5-day, then 7-day walkouts ran through 2023. At peak, the April 2024 strike by resident doctors and consultants coincided for a 'whole hospital' action. Total: 44 days of strike between March 2023 and July 2024. The Sunak government offered 8.8%+6% (cumulative 14%) in spring 2023 — rejected. Labour's election meant a reset.

**Streeting's September 2024 deal.** On 16 September 2024 Wes Streeting and BMA Junior Doctors Committee chair Robert Laurenson agreed: 22.3% cumulative pay increase over 2023-24 and 2024-25 combined (10.9% + 4.05% plus fixed uplifts), immediate implementation, and a commitment to a Review Body process reform. BMA members ratified in a 66% Yes vote (turnout 71%). Total cost of the settlement around £1.2bn per year, funded via NHS contingency and the autumn budget.

**Consultants.** The BMA Consultants Committee also struck in July, August and September 2023 — the first consultant strikes since the 1970s. Settled in March 2024 with a 4.95% uplift and a review-body process review. Specialty and Associate Specialist doctors (SAS) similarly settled.

**Ambulance, radiographers, physios.** GMB, Unison and Unite ambulance workers struck in late 2022 / early 2023; the Society of Radiographers struck in July 2023; physiotherapists in early 2023. All settled within the wider Agenda for Change pay envelope. Scotland avoided most action via devolved higher awards; Wales had parallel settlements. Northern Ireland had prolonged disputes through 2023.

**The operational cost.** NHS England estimated 1.5 million appointments were cancelled over the 2023-24 dispute period, adding to already-backlogged elective waiting lists. The 18-week referral-to-treatment standard, already breached, deteriorated further. NHS Providers put the cumulative staff-cost impact (cover payments, agency rates, cancelled theatre cover) at over £3bn across 2022-23 and 2023-24 combined.

**What it changed.** The resolution pattern had three features: (1) a Labour government willing to negotiate, ending the Sunak/Barclay standoff; (2) a multi-year settlement rather than an annual one; (3) a commitment to Review Body reform — the DHB Review Body and the Doctors' and Dentists' Review Body have long been criticised as constrained by Treasury remit letters. Whether the 2024 settlements hold depends on the 2025-26 award (3.6% for AfC, similar for doctors). Inflation running below the earnings lock implies smaller awards in 2025-26; real-terms standstill has a way of re-opening disputes.
